answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents surveying karst caves or reef ecosystems to hash their public key and an epoch beacon through a large DRAM buffer mixed by a stream cipher until meeting a target. Because each solution binds to one key, an attacker incurs a verifiable cost in memory bandwidth and compute energy per identity. However, wealthy adversaries renting server clusters can still outspend honest operators.
